panels.description: The Java SDK's Micrometer timers publish histogram buckets only up to 30s, so p95 cannot report a value above 30s: anything slower shows as exactly 30s. The max series comes from the timer's own `_max` gauge, which covers the last few minutes and has no ceiling.

panels.title: Long Poll Latency (avg / max)
panels.description: Poll{Workflow,Activity,Nexus}TaskQueue are long polls. An idle poll waits for the server's poll timeout (about 60s) and then returns empty, so values near 60s mean idle pollers, not slowness. Short polls mean the poll picked up a task. The histogram buckets stop at 30s, so p95 would stay pinned at 30s; this panel uses sum/count for the mean and the `_max` gauge for the recent maximum.

The Java SDK's Micrometer timers publish histogram buckets only up to 30s, so p95 cannot report a value above 30s: anything slower shows as exactly 30s. The max series comes from the timer's own `_max` gauge, which covers the last few minutes and has no ceiling.

targets.expr:
(sum by (namespace, service, worker_type, task_queue) (temporal_worker_task_slots_used{namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"$service"}) + sum by (namespace, service, worker_type, task_queue) (temporal_worker_task_slots_available{namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"$service"}))
and on (namespace, service, worker_type, task_queue) (sum by (namespace, service, worker_type, task_queue) (max_over_time(temporal_worker_task_slots_used{namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Slots Used (sampled peak) vs Capacity
panels.description: **used** (solid): highest `temporal_worker_task_slots_used` reading in each interval, summed across worker instances. **capacity** (dashed): `slots_used + slots_available`, the same number of slots the *Slots Available* panel counts down from. When used approaches capacity, the worker type is saturated. Because these come from the gauge they are correct for long-running tasks, but the 15s scrape rarely catches millisecond tasks in flight (see *Avg Busy Slots*). Series that are idle (0 used) are hidden.

targets.expr: (sum by (namespace, service, worker_type, task_queue) (rate(temporal_workflow_task_execution_latency_seconds_sum{namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])) or sum by (namespace, service, worker_type, task_queue) (rate(temporal_activity_execution_latency_seconds_sum{namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])) or sum by (namespace, service, worker_type, task_queue) (rate(temporal_local_activity_execution_latency_seconds_sum{namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval])) or sum by (namespace, service, worker_type, task_queue) (rate(temporal_nexus_task_execution_latency_seconds_sum{namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"$service"}[$__rate_interval]))) > 0

panels.title: Avg Busy Slots (from execution time)
panels.description: Seconds of task execution per second, from the execution latency `_sum` counters of workflow, activity, local activity and Nexus tasks. By Little's law this equals the average number of busy slots, and it counts tasks of any length, including millisecond ones the slot gauge never catches. Counters only increase when a task completes, so long-running tasks show up as a spike at completion; use *Slots Used vs Capacity* for those. Idle series are hidden.
